title: ByteDance Plans to Take on Meta's Muse, Eyes Rival AI Agent Launch In Coming Weeks: Report
summary: ByteDance plans to launch rival AI agent in coming weeks
detailed: ByteDance plans to release a new AI assistant in the coming weeks to compete with U.S. counterparts, a strategy outlined by co-founder Zhang Yiming during a recent all-hands meeting.
Meta's competing Muse AI app surpassed 10.4 million downloads by mid-October 2025, driven by Meta's 3.64 billion daily active users across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.
ByteDance aims to compete with firms like Anthropic and OpenAI long-term, estimating completion by 2029 or 2030.
This matters as it highlights intensifying global competition among major tech platforms to scale consumer AI assistants and enterprise sales operations.
sentences: ByteDance Ltd. reportedly plans the release of an AI assistant on the lines of Meta Platforms Inc.
META in the coming weeks to advance its lead in the AI race with the U.S. counterparts.
Co-founder Zhang Yiming briefed researchers, engineers, as well as supporting staff about the plan in a recent all-hands meeting, chalking out key priorities, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday.
He eyes to compete with top tech firms like Anthropic and OpenAI , but cautioned that the completion would happen by 2029 or 2030.
ByteDance did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments.
Meta launched Muse AI App in September.

By mid-October, the app surpassed 10.4 million downloads, with the U.S. downloads outpacing those of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Sora, partly benefiting from Meta’s massive user base across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.
During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta’s family of apps now reaches 3.64 billion daily users.

He highlighted Muse’s early momentum and stated, “we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling.” However, Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management warned that Muse is already burning cash at an alarming rate.
Earlier this week, reports indicated that the company is planning to launch its Muse AI assistant to British users and build a sales team to sell its AI products to businesses.
